english.title: Pedestrian fail to stop when directed by an accredited person while escorting load - Police Reform Act
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in contravention of a direction to stop given by a person accredited under the Police Reform Act 2002 engaged in the regulation of traffic on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..), while escorting a

(A)_[vehicle]_
(B)_[vehicle and trailer]_

carrying a load of exceptional dimensions, you proceeded

(C)_[across]_
(D)_[along]_

the carriageway as a pedestrian
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 9 of Schedule 5 to the Police Reform Act 2002, section 37 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

english.notes:
(i) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(ii) See also other offence wordings in relation to the duties of accredited persons:-
H4915 - failed to give name and address to accredited person - relevant offence
H4943 - fail to give name/address to accredited person - act in anti-social manner
H4944 - contravene accredited person's requirement to surrender liquor
H4945 - contravene accredited person's requirement not to consume liquor
H4946 - fail to stop vehicle as directed by an accredited person while escorting load
H4947 - drive vehicle - fail to proceed as directed by an accredited person while escorting load

other.powersofarrest: An accredited person DOES NOT have a power of arrest or to detain - however as with any criminal offence a police officer may arrest without warrant.
other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
